<reason>CON made the debate easier to decide: hydrology tracks litres, not deeds, and PRO never reconciled trusting volumetric caps against farms, fabs, and breweries while treating bottlers as uniquely ungovernable. PRO’s civic-inventory frame and local-collapse argument stayed live and vivid, but CON’s usufructuary-rights answer to drought cutoffs and the product-versus-input enforcement hole left the ban looking like a gesture. PRO’s pressure Q2 was partly dodged; that kept it competitive rather than a rout.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Rebuttal 2: if caps can restrain the biggest withdrawers, they can restrain bottling; PRO’s later reliance on policing “sham flavoring” revived the discretionary capture problem PRO had called fatal.</best_rebuttal>
